div.l: Grete chere made oure oste to vs euerichone
And to þe souꝑper he set vs and that a none
He serued vs with vitaill atte beste
Strong was þe wine and wel to drink vs list
A semeleche man oure oste was with all
For to haue ben̄ an vssher of a hall
A large man was he with yen stepe
A fairer burgeis was none in chepe
Bold of his speche and wis and wel I tauȝt
And of manhode lakked him right nouȝt
Eke þereto he was a meri man̄
And aftre souꝑper to plei he began̄
And spak of mirthe amonge oþer thinges
Whan þat we had made oure rekenynges
And seid thus lordingꝭes truly
Ye ben̄ welcome to me hertely
For be my trouth if þat I shuld not lye
I ne saw þis yere so meri a companye
At ones in this herborogh as is nowe
Fayne I wol do you mirth wist y how
And of myrth I am right wel be þoght
To do you ese and it shal cost yow noght
Ye goon to Caunterbury god you spede
The blesful marter quyte youre mede
And wel I wote as ye gon bi þe wey
Ye shapen you to talken and pley
For truli confort ne mirth is none
To ride bi þe wei as dome as stone
And þerefor wol I make you som disporte
As I seid erst and do you som conforte
And if it like you al be oon assent
For to stonde at my iugement
And for to werche right as I shal sey
To morow whan ye riden bi þe wey
Now be my faders soule þat is dede
But if ye be meri I gif you my hede
Hold vp youre hondes with oute more speche
Oure counsell was not longe to seche
He thought not to make it wise
And graunted him with oute mor avise
And bade him sei his verdite as him liste
Lordinꝭes qduod he now herkeneth þe beste
But taketh it not I prai you in disdayne
